svg.text: FraudCNNResAttn — Data Flow Through the Network
batch=512 · window=20 · features=244 · channels=128 · res_blocks=3 · heads=4 · dropout=0.2
Last 20 transactions per UID, each a 244-dim standardized feature vector (clipped to [-5, 5]). Left-padded; `lengths` says how many are real.
2. Transpose feature axis to channel axis
3. Conv1D stem ─ nn.Conv1d(in=244, out=128, kernel=3, padding=1) → BatchNorm1d(128) → ReLU

g.text: Kernel of width 3 slides along the TIME axis:
kernel w ∈ ℝ¹²⁸ˣ²⁴⁴ˣ³ (64 of them are bias-free; we have 128)
each cell = ReLU(BN(Σ over 244 chans × 3 steps))

svg.text: 4. ResNet1D stack — ResBlock1D × 3 (channels and time preserved)
5. Transpose to (B, T, C) + learnable positional encoding
(512, 128, 20) → (512, 20, 128) then h = h + pos where pos ∈ ℝ¹ˣ²⁰ˣ¹²⁸

g.text: row t = "how much does timestep t attend to each of the 20"
each timestep = weighted blend of all 20 V-vectors
Padded positions get attention score → −∞ → 0 in softmax

svg.text: 7. Masked Mean Pool over the real timesteps
padded positions contribute zero — only real transactions are averaged
same output shape as FraudLSTM — drop-in compatible
BCEWithLogitsLoss receives raw logits (sigmoid fused inside loss)
same loop as FraudLSTM — only the model class changes
Inside ONE ResBlock1D — where the skip lives
Inside ONE attention head (4 heads share the work; d_head = 128/4 = 32)

g.text: Q = h · W_Q (B, 20, 32) "what I'm looking for"
All 4 head outputs are concatenated → (B, 20, 128) → W_O.
Example attention row for t = 19 (last txn):
The last timestep can decide it cares about, say, t=17 and t=19
most (a recent burst) — something a 1-D CNN with k=3 couldn't
do in a single layer because its receptive field is only 3.
